title: FINIS: even if the crowd sometimes took signs for gods, the institutors’ relative cult still violates the likeness-ban—so say the primitive Doctors
source_text: L. Quicquid ergo esse possit de rudi & stolida plebe, quae forte, inter Ethnicos, simulachra quandoque, tanquam si essent ipsa numina, suspexerit; saltem qui Ethnicam superstitionem instituerant atque tuebantur, Non censebant, ut idem Arnobius loquitur, auri argentique materias esse per se Deos, & religiosa numina, sed ex his Deos colebant, & in iis numen ipsum Venerabantur. Adeoque, licet peccaverint contra Dei mandatum, Non habebis Deos alienos coram me, quando vero Deo, falsos alios adjunxerunt, dici tamen non possunt, in fabricatione & cultu imaginum, transgressi esse interdictum illud de nulla similitudine colenda atque facienda, si tantum per illud vetamur, imagines ut Deos habere & colere; cum nihilominus, non obstantibus istis eorum coloribus & excusationibus quas referunt, prisci Ecclesiae Doctores interdictum istud graviter violasse, ab iis censantur.
pass_a_gloss: Whatever therefore may be of the rude and stupid crowd, which perhaps, among the Ethnics, sometimes looked up to simulacra as if they were the divinities themselves; at least those who had instituted and were guarding Ethnic superstition did not judge, as the same Arnobius speaks, that the materials of gold and silver are Gods per se, and religious divinities, but from these they cultivated Gods, and in them they Venerated the divinity itself. And accordingly, although they sinned against God’s commandment, Thou shalt not have alien Gods before me, when to the true God they joined other false ones, yet they cannot be said, in the fabrication and cult of images, to have transgressed that interdict concerning no likeness to be cultivated and made, if by that we are forbidden only to hold and cultivate images as Gods; although nevertheless, those colors and excuses of theirs which they report not withstanding, the primitive Doctors of the Church judge that they gravely violated that interdict.
pass_b_english: Institutors of pagan cult knew gold is not God per se—they venerated divinity through it.
Alien-gods precept may catch their false companions; the likeness-ban still catches their relative image-work if Rome’s narrow reading stands—yet the Fathers say they broke that interdict badly.
Pars altera closes here; next frontier is Angelorum & Hominum Sanctorum Cultu.

lemmas.gloss: that they gravely violated that interdict

choices.english: the primitive Doctors of the Church
choices.why: Closing patristic verdict against relative pagan cult.
